notes: Main disagreements: (1) policy_type between neighbouring types: P56/P07 and P56/P61 for background and scope sentences, P19/P01 for default bans (resolved by whether the rule is the default or an instructor-chosen template), P32/P41 and P39/P40 for advice and caution sentences, and P35 versus UNCOVERED for a general citation requirement; resolved by re-reading the sentence and not inferring unstated purposes. (2) phase, mostly before-course versus during-work for instructor design advice, and during-assessment versus course-start for the instructor's advance exception; set by the act the sentence describes. (3) modality, should versus may for 'consider' advice and informs versus must for declarative sentences. (4) Actor student versus all on a few scope/default sentences. Both coders gave delegates for both documents. Only-one-coder units were real statements and kept (A: 6 in the 2026 guidelines, 1 in the faculty letter; B: 1 and 2); A's three additional units that restated the same sentence (scholarship citation, a repeated skills-loss rationale, and the examples list of unsubmitted uses) were dropped. B coded the 'You may not submit' sentence twice because the text repeats it in two templates; both were kept and matched to A's units.
